q: What was David’s one condition for making a covenant with Abner?
a: Abner had to bring his wife Michal, Saul’s daughter, when he came to see David.

q: What price had David paid for Michal to be his wife?
a: David had paid the price of 100 Philistine foreskins for Michal.

q: Why did Uriah say he would not go to his own house?
a: Uriah said he would never go to his house to eat, drink, and lie with his wife while the Box, Israel, and Judah were dwelling in tents, and Joab and his men were camping in the open field.

q: What did Yahweh say David had done?
a: Yahweh said David had struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, had taken his wife to be his own wife, and had murdered him with the sword of the Ammonites. Yahweh said that David did not take seriously what he commanded when he said that his people must not commit adultery or murder. David did things that Yahweh considers to be very evil!

q: What did Yahweh say would happen because David despised him and took Uriah’s wife?
a: Yahweh said that he would make someone from David’s own family cause disaster for him. Yahweh would take David’s wives away from him and give them to that person instead. He will have sexual relations with them in public.

q: What did Amnon do to get to see Tamar?
a: Amnon pretended to be sick, and when David came to see him, he asked David to let Tamar come and make food for him so he could eat from her hand.

q: How were the two men helped?
a: The man’s wife spread a covering over the well and spread grain on it, and when Absalom’s servants asked where the men were, she told them they had crossed the brook.

q: What are the last words of David said to be?
a: They are the oracle of David, the man raised to a high position, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the one who wrote beautiful songs for the people of Israel.
